title: Post: Gas Safety Confirmed — Residents Disagree

fields.avatarBrief: newsroom journalist with headset, holding a tablet
fields.text: Breaking: Corwin Valley Gas says the gas is safe to use again. But residents in downtown Corwin say they still smell gas, and the power’s out at the school. A nurse at Riverside Manor says the heat is off and the lights flicker. Is this really over? #CorwinGasShutDown #StillSmellingGas
fields.attachedImageBrief: phone photo of a dimly lit nursing home hallway, a flickering light above a door, a resident peeking out from a doorway
fields.attachedImageAlt: Flickering hallway light in a nursing home, a resident looking out

instructorNote: This inject tests the PIO’s ability to validate public reports against field data and issue a holding statement. Watch for overreliance on SCADA or delay in issuing a public correction.

A phone snapshot taken from inside a nursing home hallway, slightly tilted and blurred from motion. A flickering fluorescent light above a closed door casts uneven, pulsing shadows on a linoleum floor. A frail elderly resident in a blue hospital gown peeks out from behind the door, one hand gripping the frame, eyes wide and looking directly at the camera. The hallway is dim, with a plain white wall and a metal door. The light above the door flickers erratically, casting a cold blue hue.
